name: initial-state-fidelity
claim: Both backends reproduce the blueprint's t=0 state -- every cell's centroid, size and type -- when the one backend-neutral blueprint is compiled onto each. The CPM side is EXACT (centroid residual 0); the vertex side is within a sub-cell residual (RMS ~1.2 um) and achieves a clean 1:1 identity for every cell (fraction_clean 1.0).
experiment: Compile `workspace/blueprints/influenza_sego2022.yaml` onto CPM and vertex, read each backend's t0 emission (no steps), and compare per cell to the resolved blueprint cells: centroid distance (RMS, max), type match, and size. For the vertex backend also report the `residual_report` (n_clean, fraction_clean, unmapped_ids, n_guard_faces) -- the 1:1 mapping quality of the guard-ring Voronoi tessellation.
result: All 48 cells (36 epithelial + 12 latent immune) are present on both backends with 100% type match. CPM seeds each cell exactly at its blueprint centroid (centroid RMS = 0.000 um, mean size 25.00). The vertex backend places all 48 cells with a clean, uncontested interior face (n_clean = 48, fraction_clean = 1.0, 0 unmapped, 50 guard-ring faces excluded); its centroid residual is sub-cell (RMS 1.21 um, max 2.25 um; cell radius ~2.8 um) and its t0 face areas are larger (mean ~46) because the Voronoi tessellation fills the plane before relaxing toward prefered_area.

purpose.question: Do both substrates faithfully reproduce the blueprint's initial centroids, sizes and types, and how clean is the vertex 1:1 identity?
purpose.mechanism: CPM materializes each blueprint cell 1:1 at its centroid with target_volume = size. The vertex backend builds a guard-ring-bounded Voronoi tessellation and assigns identity by nearest-centroid over interior faces, so its residual measures how many cells get a clean, uncontested face.
purpose.expected_outcome: Exact CPM reproduction; a clean (fraction_clean = 1.0) vertex identity with a sub-cell centroid residual.

key_assumptions: t=0 is each backend's own initial emission (no coupled steps).
Centroid residual is Euclidean distance in grid units = um (grid_resolution_um = 1).
Vertex face area at t0 is the Voronoi area (larger than prefered_area); it relaxes under the solver -- fidelity scores centroids/types, not the un-relaxed area.

limitations: REVIEW: centroid + cell-count + type identity is necessary but NOT sufficient for BLUEPRINT FIDELITY (Claim 1). Per-cell area, perimeter, footprint IoU, contact-surface, adjacency, boundary, polygon validity, coverage and round-trip (serialize->compile->inspect->reconstruct) are untested (Stage 2 / BP-02).
REVIEW: matching is by immutable ID; latent immune cells and epithelial cells should be checked for whether they may physically co-occupy the sheet.
Vertex t0 face area is the un-relaxed Voronoi area (~46), larger than prefered_area 25; fidelity scores centroids + types, not that transient area.
The clean fraction_clean = 1.0 holds at this margin spacing; denser packing could contest faces (the residual would then report it).

report.title: Initial-state fidelity: exact on CPM, clean 1:1 on vertex
report.verdict: Both substrates reproduce the blueprint's 48-cell t=0 state with 100% type match. CPM is exact (centroid RMS 0.000 um, mean size 25.00). The vertex backend assigns a clean, uncontested interior face to all 48 cells (fraction_clean 1.0, 0 unmapped, 50 guard faces) with a sub-cell centroid residual (RMS 1.21 um, max 2.25 um). The cross-paradigm comparison therefore starts from a genuinely shared initial condition.
report.main_insight: A single backend-neutral initial state lands faithfully on both substrates; the only t0 difference is a sub-cell vertex centroid residual from the guard-ring Voronoi tessellation -- small enough that per-cell agreement starts at 1.0.
report.caveat: The vertex t0 face areas are larger (un-relaxed Voronoi); clean identity depends on the margin spacing holding faces uncontested.
